headline: A closed growth plate
body: Spinal growth plate function was reactivated in an animal model.
punch: Which raises a question this field usually treats as settled.

headline: Closure is discussed
body: The plate fuses, growth ends, the window shuts. That framing is the reason so much content is about beating a deadline.
punch: The spine may be less final than the limbs.

headline: The technique
body: A scoliosis correction method that works by modulating growth — applying mechanical constraint to one side of the spine so it grows asymmetrically.
punch: Designed to steer growth, not to restart it.

headline: The unexpected result
body: In an animal model, tethering reactivated vertebral growth plate function — suggesting closure or dormancy in the spine may be more reversible than assumed.
punch: Mechanical input restarting a biological process.

headline: Which matters mechanistically
body: If a growth plate can be pushed back into function, then closure is a state rather than an event. States can in principle be changed. Events cannot.
punch: State versus event is not a semantic difference.

headline: But note
body: Vertebral growth plates differ from long bone plates in structure, loading and growth pattern. Spinal results do not transfer to femurs by default.

headline: And note
body: The intervention was load, not a molecule. Nothing here suggests a compound reactivates growth plates, and that's the version most likely to be invented.
punch: Load did this. Not a drug.

headline: The honest framing
body: One animal model, one bone type, one mechanical intervention. It's a real crack in a claim treated as absolute — not a route to more height.
punch: A crack in a certainty is not an opportunity.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
